findings.reason: Untrusted source: interface descriptor data supplied at USB enumeration by a physically attacker-controlled gadget. In qmi_wwan_bind (line 744) info->control starts as the probed interface; a CDC Union descriptor's bSlaveInterface0 can move info->data to a different interface, leaving info->control == intf while info->data != info->control. qmi_wwan_register_subdriver (line 686, called from bind at line 798 during usbnet_probe) then does 'dev->status = &info->control->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0];' (line 699) with no bNumEndpoints >= 1 check for the control altsetting. Per drivers/usb/core/config.c usb_parse_interface (lines 612-627), when bNumEndpoints == 0 the alt->endpoint array is never allocated and stays NULL (kzalloc only when num_ep > 0), so &endpoint[0] evaluates to a null-based pointer and dev->status->desc is dereferenced immediately at line 711 (usb_cdc_wdm_register(info->control, &dev->status->desc, ...)) - a NULL-pointer dereference at probe triggered by device plug-in. Reachability: the id table matches class-based entries like USB_VENDOR_AND_INTERFACE_INFO(HUAWEI_VENDOR_ID, USB_CLASS_VENDOR_SPEC, 1, 9) (qmi_wwan.c ~lines 979-996) and QMI_MATCH_FF_FF_FF, which match on interface class regardless of endpoint count; qmi_wwan_probe (line 1530) only rejects bNumEndpoints == 2 (diag interface, line 1570) and never requires >= 1 endpoint on the control interface, so a gadget declaring a vendor-spec control interface with zero endpoints and a separate union-referenced data interface reaches the read. Unsafe use: the endpoint descriptor is passed to usb_cdc_wdm_register and dev->status feeds usbnet status URB logic (init_status). Counterevidence checked: for the single-interface case (control == data) usbnet_get_endpoints (usbnet.c:90-142) requires an in+out bulk pair, so it is protected; cdc_ether.c:305 guards its identical endpoint[0] read with 'bNumEndpoints == 1', showing the expected validation pattern that qmi_wwan lacks; usbnet.c:1854 post-bind check only validates bulk endpoints on the data interface, not the control interface's endpoint[0]; usb_parse_interface itself only warns when actual endpoint descriptors differ from bNumEndpoints (config.c:646-650), it does not force an allocation.
findings.conclusion: qmi_wwan_bind path reads control interface endpoint[0] with no bNumEndpoints check (qmi_wwan.c:699); a gadget with a zero-endpoint vendor-spec control interface makes endpoint[] NULL, dereferenced at usb_cdc_wdm_register (line 711), crashing probe on plug-in.

candidates.reason: usbpn_probe explicitly validates data_intf->altsetting[0]/[1] bNumEndpoints combinations (lines 344-351) to be 0/2 or 2/0 before reading endpoint[0]/[1] (lines 369-378).
endpoint[0] read is guarded by 'if (info->control->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints == 1)' at line 305, and the endpoint is then validated as int-in with sufficient wMaxPacketSize.
probe checks 'if (intf->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints < 3) return -ENODEV' at line 4689 before endpoint[2] access, and validates bulk in/out via usb_pipe_endpoint.
hso_get_ep and hso_get_mux_ports iterate 'for (i = 0; i < iface->desc.bNumEndpoints; i++)' (lines 3145, 3166) so all endpoint[i] accesses are bounded by the descriptor-declared count.
probe loops 'for (i = 0; i < hintf->desc.bNumEndpoints; i++)' (line 606) over usb_altnum_to_altsetting result and rejects missing bulk in/out endpoints before use.
usbnet_get_endpoints iterates 'for (ep = 0; ep < alt->desc.bNumEndpoints; ep++)' per altsetting and returns -EINVAL unless an in and out bulk endpoint were found.
cdc_ncm_find_endpoints loops ep over cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints before reading endpoint + ep.
sierra_net_bind requires numendpoints == 3 (lines 666-672) before usbnet_get_endpoints and requires a non-NULL status endpoint.
qmi_wwan_probe only rejects bNumEndpoints == 2 (diag interface); it imposes no lower bound on the control interface that bind later indexes at endpoint[0] (see finding at line 699).
probe rejects 'bNumEndpoints < 2' at line 1309 and iterates endpoint[r] bounded by the descriptor count, then requires bulk/int endpoints via usb_find_common_endpoints.
endpoint loop is bounded by bNumEndpoints (line 1070) and probe then requires all expected endpoints via usb_check_bulk_endpoints/usb_check_int_endpoints (lines 1089-1102).

brcmf_usb_probe needs vendor-spec interface (class 0xff/2/0xff) and loops ep over desc->bNumEndpoints, then fails with -ENODEV when no in/out bulk endpoint was found, so fixed assumed indices are never used.

coverage_gaps: Remaining drivers/net/wireless USB NIC loops (ath10k, ath6kl, at76c50x, ar5523, libertas, libertas_tf, mt76, mt7601u, mwifiex, p54usb, rt2x00, rtl8xxxu, rtlwifi, rtw88, rsi, zd1211rw) were confirmed bNumEndpoints-bounded by grep line evidence, not by full-function reads.

drivers/net/usb drivers using hardcoded pipe numbers with usb_pipe_endpoint() (e.g. lan78xx BULK_IN_PIPE) other than lan78xx were not individually re-read; only their grep-visible patterns were checked.
cdc_mbim.c, huawei_cdc_ncm.c, hso.c control-interface paths beyond the endpoint loops were only spot-checked for status-endpoint endpoint[0]-style reads.
drivers/net/wwan (iosm, mhi, rpmsg, t7xx) contains no USB interface descriptor-array access (PCIe/MHI/rpmsg only), but this was established by a single directory-wide grep, not file-by-file review.
limitations: No runtime reproducer or compile test was run; the qmi_wwan NULL-deref hypothesis rests on static reading of qmi_wwan.c plus the drivers/usb/core/config.c usb_parse_interface allocation path (alt->endpoint left NULL when bNumEndpoints == 0).

Actual exploitability of the class-based Huawei/Quectel ID entries with a zero-endpoint control interface depends on usbcore matching order and cdc_parse_cdc_header behavior, which were reviewed statically but not exercised.
Legacy Fact cards for sibling snapshots (i003/i007/i011/i015/i019/i023/i027/i035) were unavailable for cross-comparison; conclusions here cover snapshot s08 only.
